topic.title: Redoing Translations
topic.shortdesc: How to make the agent retranslate content, either a few files or a whole project, after you change your source, terminology, instructions, or validation rules.

body.p: The agent skips any file it considers current, so to redo a translation you reset the state recorded for that file in the translation index. Once a file looks missing or stale again, the next translation job picks it up.

section.title: Retranslate Specific Files
section.p: To force the agent to retranslate a file, delete its recorded state from .contentfusion/i18n/translation-index.xml:

ul.li: Delete the <entry> for that file in a given language, and the file becomes missing for that language and is retranslated on the next job.
Delete every <entry> for the file to retranslate it into all languages.

section.title: Start Over After Changing Your Guidance
section.p: When a translation does not come out the way you want, you often fix the cause once and regenerate the affected content, for example after you correct your terminology file, refine agent-instructions.md, or adjust your validation rules. Changing this guidance does not make existing translations stale on its own, because staleness tracks only whether the English source changed. A normal job therefore skips those files, so you reset their recorded state to pick them up again:

ul.li: To redo everything, delete the whole translation index, or the fragment that covers the content you want to regenerate. Every source file it recorded becomes missing and is retranslated on the next job.
To redo a subset, delete only the entries for the files or languages you want regenerated.

section.p: Then run translation again and review the result as usual. See Reviewing Translations Before You Commit.
section.note: Deleting an entry discards the recorded link between a source file and its translation, not the translated file on disk, and the next job overwrites that file with fresh output. Commit or back up any manual corrections you want to keep before you rerun the translation.
